title: Vellum AI Alternatives in 2026, Sorted by Job
summary: Vellum AI alternatives vary by job: prompt testing, workflow automation, or evaluation. Match your specific need to find the right tool.
body_markdown:
## Connect vellum.AI to business workflows with Activepieces


If the job is automating the processes around vellum.ai rather than replacing it,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) fits, and where the data lives is a separate question from whether it fits.


Agents, integrations, flows, shared tables, an AI chat and MCP tools are one product there, under a single set of access, audit and release controls on cloud or self-hosted, and MoneyGram and Moneypenny run it in production.


Build the same span from point tools and you have six vendors and six places to reconstruct what happened when a run failed.


Nothing specific to vellum.ai ships in it (checked 2026-11-04), so there's no native integration, and every route below is a general connection method.


I haven't run vellum.ai against any of them, so read each one as a pattern to verify, not a tested recipe.


### Option 1: an HTTP request step


This is the simplest route and the easiest to audit, because the whole integration is one request you can read.


The workflow below shows the shape: a trigger fires, and a single HTTP step sends a POST with an Authorization header and a body to Square, a payments platform, to revoke an OAuth token.


According to the run details, both steps completed, so you can check the input and output JSON of each one.


Point the step at whatever endpoint vellum.ai's API documentation lists, and put the key in the header; the same pattern works there. Check the documented URL and auth scheme yourself before you build on it.


### Option 2: an AI step with a custom provider


If you want the workflow to call a model hosted behind vellum.ai as if it were any other provider, an AI step with a custom provider is the next option.


It only works if vellum.ai exposes an endpoint in a request format the step accepts. I couldn't confirm that it does.


Read the provider settings in your Activepieces version and the vellum.ai API reference side by side before committing.


### Option 3: an MCP server


Third is the Model Context Protocol (MCP), a standard for letting an AI client call tools. Here the question is whether vellum.ai, or something you place in front of it, publishes an MCP server that Activepieces can reach.


I found nothing confirming one, so treat this as the route that needs the most checking. If you build a small server yourself, the source tree is the artifact to review.
